datum_note: MSC.73(69) (1998) positions are on the old (pre-WGS 84) chart datum. Comparing the ten MSC.73(69) positions with MPA's current WGS 84 positions for the same lights and buoys: latitude agrees within 0.014', longitude is 0.089' to 0.105' larger (about 165-195 m east) in the IMO text. For a WGS 84 map use the MPA positions; Tg Piai and Pulau Karimun Kecil have no official WGS 84 version (shift them about 0.1' west only if flagged inferred). The TSS coordinates in S5 are WGS 84 (MPA inserted them; the Main Strait annex is identical to IMO COLREG.2/Circ.54, which is itself WGS 84).

area.text: Operational area: the Straits of Malacca and Singapore between longitudes 100°40'E and 104°23'E as shown on the chartlets in appendices 1 and 2; includes the routeing system; nine sectors (MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 2.1). Reference charts MAL 515, 521, 523 (para 2.2).
area.notes: On both IMO and MPA chartlets the operational area is drawn as a dashed corridor around the routeing system (TSS, precautionary areas), not the whole strait; that corridor has no published coordinates. The north and south limits of each sector are therefore unconfirmed.

SPI text says the DW route lies 'within the eastbound lane described in paragraph (d)', but (d) is the westbound lane; the positions lie in the eastbound lane (e). Text slip in the source, positions used as printed. 'Phillip Channel' is the name used in the IMO Rules (SN/Circ.198) for this DW route.

tss_status: Current text: TSS adopted at MSC 69 (COLREG.2/Circ.44, 26 May 1998, in force 1 Dec 1998), Main Strait separation zone amended by COLREG.2/Circ.54 (MSC 78, 2004; anchorage area inside the separation zone; in force 1 July 2005 after COLREG.2/Circ.54/Add.2). SPI 2026 (1 Nov 2026) and SPI 2025 (1 Feb 2025) routeing annexes are word-for-word identical and cite only Circ.44 and Circ.54, so no later amendment is known to MPA. COLREG.2/Circ.44 itself was not found online; annexes 4, 6, 7, 8 are therefore taken from MPA's official SPI (WGS 84), not checked against the IMO original.

other.item: Rules for vessels navigating through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (IMO, MSC 69, in force 1 Dec 1998, SN/Circ.198)
other.summary: Deep-draught vessel = draught 15 m or more; VLCC = tanker 150,000 DWT and above. DDVs and VLCCs keep an under-keel clearance of at least 3.5 m at all times through the whole Straits. Eastbound DDVs shall use the deep water routes and as far as practicable not overtake in the DW routes in Phillip Channel and Singapore Strait. Vessels with defects affecting safety fix them before entering. In an emergency leave the lane to starboard. Westbound vessels near Raffles Lighthouse: caution, do not impede a vessel constrained by her draught crossing to the SPM. Maximum manoeuvring readiness in precautionary areas. Rule 9(b): DDVs, VLCCs and difficult tows are advised to broadcast 8 hours before entering the TSS (name, DWT, draught, speed, times passing One Fathom Bank Lt, Raffles Lt and Horsburgh Lt).

other.item: 12 knot speed limit for VLCCs and deep-draught vessels (Rule 7), 'as far as it is safe and practicable', over the ground
other.summary: Areas: (a) One Fathom Bank TSS; (b) the deep water routes in Phillip Channel and in Singapore Strait; (c) westbound lanes between 01°12·51’N 103°52·15’E and 01°11·59’N 103°50·21’E, and between 01°11·13’N 103°49·08’E and 01°08·65’N 103°44·30’E (MPA: south of St John's Island to Raffles Lighthouse). These four positions equal TSS points (114)/(117), (112)/(107), (99)/(106) and (97).

other.item: Night signal for vessels crossing the TSS / precautionary areas in the Singapore Strait (IMO recommendatory measure, MSC 91, full measure from 1 June 2013)
other.summary: Vessels of 300 GT and above, 50 m and above, or tows of 300 GT / 50 m combined, crossing the lanes to or from ports and anchorages are recommended to show three all-round green lights in a vertical line (if carried), report the intention to VTIS in advance, and cross in ample time. Recommendatory, not mandatory.

Essential: A (name, call sign, IMO number), C or D (position), P (hazardous cargo yes/no, class), Q or R (defects, pollution). E and F (course, speed) only when the VTS asks. VHF voice, English, SMCP. Listening watch on the sector channel; general broadcasts on CH 16 after an announcement on the sector channel.

other.item: Singapore port callers: Confirmation of Arrival (MPA, national, not STRAITREP)
other.summary: Vessels 300 GT and above, tows of 300 GT combined, and passenger vessels calling at Singapore report Confirmation of Arrival to the VTIS at the same reporting points (VTIS East CH 10, Central CH 14, West CH 73): name, call sign, location, POB (passenger ships), ETA or pilot boarding ground, height if changed. Port VHF: East Control CH 12 east of 103°51.2'E, West Control CH 68 west of 103°51.2'E (port area).

other.item: Malaysian electronic STRAITREP reporting trial (sectors 1 to 6, Klang VTS), 1 May to 31 Dec 2026
other.summary: UNCONFIRMED: only press reports (Safety4Sea 19 May 2026, Seatrade 18 May 2026) seen; the Marine Department Malaysia notice itself was not found. Reported as an alternative (web portal / e-mail within 24 h before entering) to VHF; VHF reporting remains the IMO rule.

At NCSR 13 (22-26 June 2026) Malaysia submitted NCSR 13/INF.11 on a review of STRAITREP; Indonesia and Singapore commented. Information only; no amendment proposed or adopted. MSC.73(69) remains the text in force.

gaps: No official text gives coordinates for the boundaries of STRAITREP sectors 1 to 5, or the sector 5/6 boundary: only the IMO chartlet (Appendix 1). Marine Department Malaysia / Royal Malaysian Navy annual Notices to Mariners could not be downloaded (navy.mil.my returned HTTP 500).
No coordinates for the north/south limits of sectors 7, 8, 9 (the dashed corridor on the chartlets).
Tg Piai and Pulau Karimun Kecil: only the 1998 IMO positions (old datum); no official WGS 84 values found.
MPA uses both 103°44.5'E and 103°44.6'E for the sector 7/8 line on the same page (table and chartlet: 103°44.5'E).
Eastern limit: IMO 104°23'E (old datum), MPA chartlet 104°22.9'E (WGS 84), MPA table 104°23.0'E.
IMO COLREG.2/Circ.44 (26 May 1998) original not found online; TSS annexes other than the Main Strait are from MPA SPI 2026 only (official Singapore government source, WGS 84 inserted by MPA).
Inshore traffic zone outer ends (lines 'to meet the Malaysian coast') have only a start point and a bearing.
Malaysian electronic reporting trial 2026: seen only in press; official notice not found.
Indonesian sources (e.g. for Selat Riau / Selat Durian approaches) not searched beyond the IMO and MPA texts.
